finding.summary: Scope creep: the branch's stated scope is #661 (CLI error envelope as one line carrying `command`), but the change also lands an entire OAuth/cookie/login-hardening epic — `__Host-` prefixing of session/refresh cookies, a rewritten `useSecureCookies` predicate, `cliLoginAvailable()` refusals + a production-downgrade warning, HMAC-bound CLI confirm tokens, a new `packages/backend/src/logging/log-safe-url.ts` access-log redactor, the CLI launch-token indirection + `login-url.txt` + 30s→5min timeout change, and a frontend LoginForm rewrite. The branch's own task note admits it "carries two bodies of work". None of that follows from #661's outcome; each is separately reviewable and separately riskier than the envelope change it rides on.
finding.evidence: "The branch carries two bodies of work: its stated scope (#661 — the CLI error envelope as one line carrying `command`) and a CLI login-hardening epic layered on top between Aug 12–15."

verdict.reason: Every element of the presence claim checks out. The quoted evidence is verbatim in the repo: docs/tasks/active/20260820-pr786-conflict-resolution-todo.md:8-10 states the branch "carries two bodies of work: its stated scope (#661 ...) and a CLI login-hardening epic layered on top between Aug 12-15", on branch agent/661-cli-error-envelope-command (line 3). #661's own acceptance criteria (20260811-cli-error-envelope-command-todo.md:56-63) cover only single-line envelope, dotted `command`, and unchanged code/message — nothing about OAuth, cookies, or PKCE. The second epic is tracked under a different originating scope (#654/#655, RFC 8252/7636) and explicitly admits riding this branch: 20260812-cli-login-loopback-binding-todo.md:24-30 "It rides the #661 branch again (PR #786), not a separate one." Each enumerated artifact exists: cliLoginAvailable() refusal + downgrade warning (packages/backend/src/auth/github-auth.guard.ts:80, 233-271), __Host-/useSecureCookies cookie work (oauth-state.ts, auth.controller.ts:335, loopback note lines 148-150), HMAC-bound CLI confirm token (packages/backend/src/auth/cli-login-confirm.middleware.ts), the new access-log redactor (packages/backend/src/logging/log-safe-url.ts:167 with its own spec), the CLI launch-token indirection and 0600 login-url.txt (packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts armLaunch; loopback note 78-85), and the frontend login-form change for ?error=login_state (packages/frontend/src/components/login-form.tsx; loopback note 157-159). CONTRIBUTING.md:26-37/53-70 contains no rule pre-authorizing two epics on one branch, and the loopback note itself concedes the next login change starts from main on its own branch. Scope-conformance / unrequested scope creep is the first bullet of this lens's lane, so it cannot be dismissed as out-of-scope, and no guard makes it unreachable. Only the blocking judgement is debatable; the facts are not.

The doc records config/behaviour the code does not have — and the branch's own lessons note says the separation was done "without a new env var", contradicting the row.
finding.evidence: grep OAUTH_STATE_SECRET → only docs/design/backend.md:757, packages/backend/README.md:25, .agent-review artefacts; grep -i hkdf in packages/backend/src → no matches; oauth-state.ts:165 createWebOAuthState uses randomBytes + hashSecret (unkeyed)

verdict.reason: Every element of the finding checks out against the tree. docs/design/backend.md:757 does document an `OAUTH_STATE_SECRET` env var defaulting to "HKDF of JWT_SECRET" / "derived from JWT_SECRET with a fixed label", and packages/backend/README.md:25-34 repeats the story. Nothing implements it: repo-wide grep for OAUTH_STATE_SECRET hits only those two docs plus .agent-review artefacts (never packages/backend/src), and case-insensitive grep for hkdf in the backend source yields no matches (only vendored .trusted/scripts/agent/node_modules/fast-sha256 and lesson notes). There is no env-schema indirection that could consume it — the neighbouring JWT_REFRESH_SECRET row is read by literal name at packages/backend/src/auth/auth.service.ts:53, and the only config modules are file.config.ts / image.config.ts. The state binding is genuinely unkeyed: oauth-state.ts:165-168 createWebOAuthState uses randomBytes(32) + hashSecret, and hashSecret (oauth-state.ts:266-268) is a bare unkeyed createHash('sha256'); the verify path (line 184) mirrors it. The only createHmac uses are the Yorkie webhook guard (document/yorkie-signature.guard.ts:53) and cli-login-confirm.middleware.ts:104, which keys off the per-request cookie secret, not any derived state key. The branch's own lessons note (docs/tasks/active/20260811-cli-error-envelope-command-lessons.md:64) says HKDF separates the keys "without a new env var", contradicting the documented optional variable. Under the design-fit lens this is a design-doc-discipline defect: the canonical subsystem doc's Environment Configuration table records config and key-derivation behaviour the code does not have, misleading operators into setting a silently-ignored var and misdescribing the auth architecture. That is a factual doc/code divergence, not a taste preference, so major stands; I found no guard or alternate implementation to refute it.

verdict.reason: The row is genuinely absent from docs/design/backend.md:751-770, but the finding's premise that this table is "the canonical env list" is false, so the gap is a minor doc-tidiness nit rather than a design-fit violation. (a) The table is demonstrably non-exhaustive: grepping GITHUB_AUTHORIZATION_URL|FILE_STORAGE_PREFIX|IMAGE_STORAGE_PREFIX|YORKIE_SECRET_KEY|WAFFLEBASE_KAFKA_TOPIC against backend.md returns zero matches, though all are shipped backend vars documented in packages/backend/README.md:42-114 — ~12 omissions, including the sibling auth var GITHUB_AUTHORIZATION_URL. (b) The canonical operator env list is packages/backend/README.md, where COOKIE_SECURE has a full 17-line entry (lines 54-70) covering precedence, default derivation and when to set true; repo convention confirms this is the list that gets updated for new vars (docs/tasks/archive/2026/07/20260717-share-link-analytics-todo.md:932 says "Add to packages/backend/README.md env table", and those WAFFLEBASE_* vars appear there and never in backend.md's table). (c) The design doc does document the knob substantively, not just in passing: backend.md:474-490 is a dedicated paragraph on useSecureCookies() precedence, __Host- naming and COOKIE_SECURE=true as the TLS-edge escape hatch, plus 155-172 and 441-447; operator docs cover it at packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md:135,140. (d) CONTRIBUTING.md imposes no requirement that env vars appear in a design-doc table; the design-doc discipline rule (update the canonical subsystem doc, no parallel doc) was satisfied. Not a missing/parallel doc, not a duplicated module, not a Non-Goal breach, and no acceptance criterion ties to this table — so real but non-blocking under this lens.

verdict.reason: Verified independently: `outputError` only emits `command` when a `Command` is passed (formatter.ts:158-163 → errorEnvelope at 129-137; no module-level fallback). `ctx list` (ctx.ts:85) and `status` (status.ts:69) call `outputError(e)` with no command, even though both actions are `function (this: Command)` and already use `this` (ctx.ts:72, status.ts:62). The last-resort catch in cli.ts:80-100 cannot cover them because both swallow the throw locally. This fails the issue's stated acceptance criterion "It carries `command` with the dotted command name" (docs/tasks/active/20260811-cli-error-envelope-command-todo.md:56-60) and contradicts docs/design/cli.md §9 (lines 1492-1504, plus line 1007 which says `ctx list` emits the standard envelope); the only documented exemptions are parse-time USAGE errors (cli.md:916-917) and `login` (cli.md:1508-1511). The inconsistency is visible inside ctx.ts itself, where `ctx switch` does attribute via `commandPath(this)` (ctx.ts:93,102-114) and is asserted in ctx.test.ts:136-142. Reachable paths: INVALID_FORMAT for both commands and NOT_LOGGED_IN for `ctx list` (status.test.ts:168-185 asserts only `.error.code`, never `command`). Major spec-conformance gap under the design-fit rubric; no counterexample found.
